summary: The mechanism is real and it is wired. All four declared falsifications were applied to a scratch copy of the tree, proved landed with git diff, and each reddened the row its criterion names (AC1 22 failed, AC2 7 failed, AC3 8 failed, AC4 3 failed against a 52-passed baseline); all four negative controls were driven too and each reddened the accepting/still-refused row it exists to protect (19, 10, 30, 4 failed). Used the feature as an author would: a fresh behaviour-bearing spec written from the engine template validates clean, the same spec with falsified_by deleted is refused BY NAME by python3 .veldo/validate.py spec at exit 1, and adding the compliant spec to specs/ left the full unit suite at 4530 passed / 0 failed, so nothing here pins this repository's current emptiness. No blocker. Eight notes, three of them substantive: the suite docstring's own 'THE ONE THING THIS FRAGMENT CANNOT ASSERT YET' paragraph is false in three separate ways at this commit; AC3's stand-down is RECORDED but never REPORTED at any surface an operator sees; and this repository's own specs/TEMPLATE.md - the file README.md and every pack spec skill name - carries neither behavior_bearing nor falsified_by and is permanently excepted from the template-sync gate, so AC4's rationale is unmet exactly where the item landed.

criteria.note: DROVE THE DECLARED FALSIFICATION. Replaced the per-criterion loop in falsification_problems with `return []` in BOTH .veldo/validate_checks.py and engine/.veldo/validate_checks.py (both, so the byte-identity row could not be the thing that reddened), proved it landed with git diff, and the suite went 52 passed -> 30 passed / 22 failed - exactly the count the docstring records - including the row the criterion names ('three criteria and no falsified_by anywhere is refused ONCE PER CRITERION'). THE NEGATIVE CONTROL WAS DRIVEN BOTH WAYS: under that mutation the AC1 accepting row stayed GREEN (so the 22 is the loop and not a module that failed to load), and under a blanket-refusal mutation (`if True:` in place of the missing-field test) the accepting row RED with 19 failed. THE WIRING IS REAL, contrary to the suite's own docstring: .veldo/validate.py:129 calls _VC.check_falsification_declared from check_spec, and a fresh behaviour-bearing spec I wrote into specs/ with its falsified_by deleted was refused by `python3 .veldo/validate.py spec` at exit 1 with the message naming criterion AC1. Removing that registration line in scratch reddens 4 rows of this suite. The refusal-names-the-criterion promise is asserted against the rendered page, not the predicate, and the live probe printed it verbatim.

DROVE THE DECLARED FALSIFICATION: deleted the two-floor test from _falsification_statement in both copies, git diff proved it landed, and the `n/a` row the criterion names went RED along with the padded row, both floor rows, the padding row, the both-floors-have-teeth row and the no-exemption-keyword row. THE NEGATIVE CONTROL: raising FALSIFICATION_MIN_CHARS to 500 reddened the accepting row ('a genuine one-sentence declaration is accepted') with 10 failed, so the floors cannot be satisfied by padding and cannot be what refuses everything. Read the code for an escape hatch and found none: no denylist, no allowlist, no exemption keyword, non-str values are the UNREADABLE cause and a real bool is not coerced. Confirmed against the real validator that behavior_bearing: yes / 1 / 'true # comment' are all refused (by check_observability where not by this check), so there is no truthy spelling that buys an exemption. TWO HONEST LIMITS, neither a defect against the criterion as written: a 24-char 4-word placeholder ('this criterion cannot be falsified') is accepted, which the criterion deliberately leaves to the review lane; and the docstring's recorded count for this mutation (8 FAILED) does not reproduce - I measure 7 - filed as F4.

DROVE THE DECLARED FALSIFICATION: made falsification_gated return True unconditionally and removed the raw presence gate in check_falsification_declared, git diff proved it landed, and the row the criterion names ('a spec that declares no behavior_bearing field carries bare criteria without being refused') went RED, 8 failed. THE NEGATIVE CONTROL: a BLANKET stand-down (falsification_gated always False) reddened 30 rows including 'in the SAME run a behaviour-bearing fixture missing its falsifications is still refused', so the stand-down is not what makes cases pass. The migration half is genuinely measured rather than pinned: the seeded five-spec corpus asserts every shape separately and its own negative control migrates the one offender and watches the numbers move; the LIVE rows assert conservation plus non-vacuity rather than today's count, and I confirmed the live measurement (211 specs, 43 behaviour-bearing, 43 compliant, 0 would_refuse, 168 stood down) and that adding a new compliant behaviour-bearing spec leaves the whole 4530-assertion suite green. TWO CLAUSES WEAKER THAN THEIR PROSE, filed as F2 and F6: 'the check reports its stand-down rather than passing silently' is evidenced only as an append to an in-process list that no command, gate stage or CLI ever reads - `python3 .veldo/validate.py all` prints nothing at all for the 168 stood-down specs - and 'the flip to refusing is a separate commit whose message states the date and the count' is met on the count (01bcdf3) but not on the date, and nothing asserts the flip commit at all.

DROVE THE DECLARED FALSIFICATION: deleted the falsified_by key line from engine/specs/TEMPLATE.md, git diff proved it landed, and 3 rows RED - the declaration row, the parsed-key row and the template-drives-the-validator row - exactly as recorded. THE NEGATIVE CONTROL is the one that matters here and it holds: replacing the key with the misspelling `falsifiable_by` reddened 4 rows INCLUDING the misspellings-are-absent row, so the declaration row is not 'some string is present in a long file'; and the row is structural (the field is a real key on every criterion when the template is read by the ONE parser) rather than a substring test, which the docstring records as a defect it caught in itself. VERIFIED THE FOUNDING MEASUREMENT independently: at eacf217^ the string 'negative control' appears 0 times in docs/method.md, 0 times in engine/specs/TEMPLATE.md and 0 times in specs/TEMPLATE.md, and 'falsified_by' 0 times in method.md. Verified the spine clause is where the criterion says it is (docs/method.md:89, inside 2.2 'The specification is the unit of work'), though the assertion only proves the strings exist somewhere in a 1503-line file. Byte-identity of .veldo/validate_checks.py and engine/.veldo/validate_checks.py confirmed. THE GAP, filed as F3: the criterion's letter names engine/specs/TEMPLATE.md and that file complies, but the template an author in THIS repository is pointed at (README.md:89, and every pack's spec skill) is specs/TEMPLATE.md, which carries neither behavior_bearing nor falsified_by nor the negative-control explanation and is permanently excepted from scripts/check_template_sync.sh, so the rationale 'a rule an author is never prompted for is a rule that survives only where somebody remembered it' is unmet in the repository the item landed in.

findings.text: The suite's own docstring paragraph 'THE ONE THING THIS FRAGMENT CANNOT ASSERT YET, stated rather than hidden' is false in three separate ways at this commit, and it is the item's ONLY record of its driven falsifications because proof/VELDO-0001/ carries no driven-falsifications.txt. (1) 'check_spec does not CALL this check' - .veldo/validate.py:129 is `errs += check_observability(path, repo_root) + _VC.check_falsification_declared(path, repo_root)`. (2) 'the registration line belongs in .veldo/validate.py, which is outside the footprint VELDO-0001 declares' - the spec's footprint lists '.veldo/validate.py' as its first entry, and the spec's own rollback clause says 'Delete the check's registration in check_spec', which presupposes it exists. (3) 'NO row here pretends the wiring exists' - four rows assert it through V.check_spec under FALSIFICATION_ENFORCED, and deleting the registration reddens all four. A reader auditing this item from its evidence would conclude the enforcement is inert when in fact `validate.py all` refuses. Behaviour is unaffected; the defect is that the record contradicts the code it records.
findings.evidence: grep -n falsif /home/dmitry/projects/veldo/.veldo/validate.py -> '129:    errs += check_observability(path, repo_root) + _VC.check_falsification_declared(path, repo_root)'. Spec footprint line 19: '- ".veldo/validate.py"'. Scratch copy with that call reduced to `check_observability(path, repo_root)` only: python3 scripts/selftest.py --suite 17_veldo_0001_falsification_declared -> 'selftest (PARTIAL, 1 of 34 suites): 74 passed, 4 failed', the four being the fixture positive-control row, the scalar row, the empty-list row and the bare-key row.

findings.text: AC3 promises 'the check reports its stand-down rather than passing silently'. What the code does is APPEND to a module-global list, and nothing in the repository ever reads it: falsification_migration_line(), which the module's own comment calls 'where a reader meets it', has zero callers outside this one test fragment, and FALSIFICATION_STANDDOWNS has none either. At the only surface an operator uses, `python3 .veldo/validate.py all` prints not one word about the 168 specs the rule stood down for - while the sibling release check in the same run prints 'release check STANDS DOWN, recorded rather than passed' by name. So the stand-down reads exactly as a pass to the operator, the assertion proves recording rather than reporting, and the comment's claim about where a reader meets the aggregate is false about the code.
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'falsification_migration_line|falsification_standdowns|FALSIFICATION_STANDDOWNS' over the repo: every hit is scripts/suites/17_veldo_0001_falsification_declared.py or the two byte-identical validate_checks.py copies (definition and comments) plus one comment in behavior_floor.py:190. python3 .veldo/validate.py all 2>&1 | grep -ic 'falsif|stood down|stand-down' -> 0, while the same output contains 'releases: release check STANDS DOWN, recorded rather than passed'. Live measurement: falsification_migration() -> stood_down 168.

findings.text: The prompt shipped into the adopter copy but not into the template this repository's own authors use, so AC4's stated rationale ('a rule an author is never prompted for is a rule that survives only where somebody remembered it') is unmet where the item landed. engine/specs/TEMPLATE.md carries behavior_bearing and falsified_by with its explanation; specs/TEMPLATE.md carries NEITHER, and instead carries an unrelated comment block that opens 'Nothing checks this'. README.md:89 tells an author here to 'copy specs/TEMPLATE.md', and every pack's spec skill says 'Draft the specification from the answers using specs/TEMPLATE.md' - which resolves to the compliant engine copy for an adopter (init lays engine/specs/TEMPLATE.md down at that path) and to the non-compliant local copy here. The divergence can never be caught: scripts/check_template_sync.sh:45 excepts specs/TEMPLATE.md permanently as 'per-repo'. AC4's footprint does not include specs/TEMPLATE.md and no assertion reads it. Same gap in engine/specs/TEMPLATE-standing.md, which the spec skills offer as the alternative template: it declares acceptance criteria and no falsified_by at all.
findings.evidence: diff specs/TEMPLATE.md engine/specs/TEMPLATE.md -> the engine copy adds the '# behavior_bearing: true' block and the falsified_by key plus its five-line explanation; grep -c falsified_by specs/TEMPLATE.md -> 0; grep -c falsified_by engine/specs/TEMPLATE-standing.md -> 0; sed -n '45p' scripts/check_template_sync.sh -> 'specs/TEMPLATE.md) return 0 ;;' under the comment 'the template carries local conventions'; README.md:89 and packs/*/skills/spec/SKILL.md:9.

findings.text: One of the eight counts the suite docstring records as MEASURED does not reproduce from the mutation its criterion declares. AC2's falsified_by is 'accept any non-empty string, dropping both the character and word floors'; the docstring records '8 FAILED'. Driving exactly that mutation gives 7. The other seven recorded counts reproduce to the digit (AC1 22, AC3 8, AC4 3, and the four negative controls 19, 10, 30, 4), which is what makes the odd one worth reporting rather than rounding away, and it matters more than usual because proof/VELDO-0001/ has no driven-falsifications.txt, so this docstring is the whole record. Neither of the two plausible readings of the mutation lands on 8: keeping the empty-string guard gives 7, removing it too gives 9.
findings.evidence: Scratch copy, the two-line floor test deleted from _falsification_statement in both validate_checks.py copies (git diff shown): python3 scripts/selftest.py --suite 17_veldo_0001_falsification_declared -> 'selftest (PARTIAL, 1 of 34 suites): 71 passed, 7 failed in 0.03s', against a 78-passed/0-failed baseline. scripts/suites/17_veldo_0001_falsification_declared.py:32-34 records '8 FAILED'.

findings.text: proof/VELDO-0001/manifest.json cites a PARTIAL selftest run as the unit evidence for all four criteria, and the runner that produced that line forbids exactly this citation. Every criterion's evidence ref is 'selftest (PARTIAL, 1 of 34 suites): 78 passed, 0 failed in 0.03s', and the last line the same run prints is 'PARTIAL RUN: no proof manifest, no evidence claim and no landing decision may cite this. Only a green bash scripts/verify.sh means done.' Nothing in the gate detects it. The underlying evidence does exist (the manifest separately records the full gate GREEN at e4ce85da9529, and I confirmed these 52 assertions run inside a green 4530-assertion gate at HEAD), so this is a record-hygiene defect rather than a missing proof - but on an item about evidence discipline it is the wrong artifact to be sloppy in, and the bundle also carries no driven-falsifications.txt for the four mutations it claims to have driven.
findings.evidence: cat proof/VELDO-0001/manifest.json -> four criteria, each with ref 'scripts/suites/17_veldo_0001_falsification_declared.py: selftest (PARTIAL, 1 of 34 suites): 78 passed, 0 failed in 0.03s'. scripts/run_scope.py:413 -> 'PARTIAL RUN: no proof manifest, no evidence claim and no landing decision may cite this'. ls proof/VELDO-0001/ -> manifest.json only.

findings.text: AC3 requires 'a separate commit whose message states the date and the count'. Commit 01bcdf3 is that commit and its message states the count three ways ('34 of 34 behaviour-bearing specs', '34 specs declare behaviour of 202, 34 already comply, 0 would be refused, 168 stand down') and the posture change, but it states no date anywhere in subject or body. Nothing asserts the flip commit at all - not its existence, not its message, not that the posture constant and the message agree - so the one clause of this item that lives in git history rather than in a file is unevidenced by construction.
findings.evidence: git log -1 --format=%B 01bcdf3 | grep -E '2026|[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}' -> no match; the message body reads 'THE FLIP, with the count VELDO-0001's AC3 requires the commit to state.' grep -rn 'FALSIFICATION_ENFORCED' over .veldo/ and scripts/ -> only the definition and comments in the two validate_checks.py copies.

findings.text: The migration posture AC3 relies on for adoption safety is a hardcoded module constant that ships REFUSING, with no per-repo override, so the reporting window AC3 promises existed only for this repository and only historically. engine/.veldo/validate_checks.py:752 is FALSIFICATION_ENFORCED = True byte-identically with the local copy, and the only way to reach the reporting posture is the `enforce` keyword, which nothing but the suite passes: no config file, no env var and no policy field reads the constant. An adopter who has already been declaring behavior_bearing: true and then installs or upgrades the engine is refused on arrival with no window to migrate - which is precisely the outcome the spec's own risk field and AC3 exist to prevent ('a rule written without a migration would redden a working repository on the day it lands'). The dominant adoption case is genuinely safe (behavior_bearing absent is byte-identically exempt, which I drove), which is why this is minor rather than major.
findings.evidence: grep -n 'FALSIFICATION_ENFORCED = ' engine/.veldo/validate_checks.py -> '752:FALSIFICATION_ENFORCED = True'; the two validate_checks.py copies are byte-identical (asserted by the suite and confirmed). grep -rn FALSIFICATION_ENFORCED .veldo/*.py scripts/*.py excluding validate_checks.py -> no hits. Refusal demonstrated live: python3 .veldo/validate.py spec on a behaviour-bearing spec without the field -> exit 1, 'criterion AC1 declares no falsified_by'.

findings.text: Two rows prove an ABSENCE by substring over live repository prose, which is the shape that reddens a gate on a benign edit. The AC4 negative control asserts that docs/method.md - 1503 lines of prose, edited by every item that touches the method - contains neither 'falsifiable_by' nor 'falsification_by'. The intent is right (pin the row to the enforced field name rather than to a spelling nobody uses), but the mechanism means the first author who documents the misspelling in order to warn against it turns the required gate red. The equivalent row over the 55-line template is acceptable; the one over method.md should be a positive assertion about the enforced name rather than a negative assertion about the whole file.
findings.evidence: scripts/suites/17_veldo_0001_falsification_declared.py:484-486, `not any(s in _FD_METHOD for s in ("falsifiable_by", "falsification_by"))` where _FD_METHOD is the entire text of docs/method.md (wc -l -> 1503). Not driven as a failure: I did not edit docs/method.md in the live tree.
